## Goal
Two deliverables before the launch post: `out/feed-photo.jpg` (1080x1350 JPEG with the magenta balloon fully in frame and undistorted) and `out/permit-filled.pdf` (filled from Ines's details, flattened).

## Action
- **Feed photo:** `launch.jpg` is 3000x2000 landscape; target 1080x1350 is portrait (0.8). I located the balloon by scanning magenta pixels (x 2352–2748, y 500–900, centroid 2549,699), cropped full-height × 1600 px anchored to the right edge (x 1400–3000) so the balloon sits in frame with margin, then resized LANCZOS to exactly 1080x1350. No stretch: crop and target share the 0.8 ratio.
- **Permit:** filled the four form fields (`organizer`, `event_date`, `location`, `attendees`), then flattened by removing the AcroForm so the fields can no longer be edited; the field values remain rendered as the widget appearance streams.

## Result
- `out/feed-photo.jpg` — 1080x1350 JPEG (verified by reloading: `out.size = (1080, 1350)`; visual check above shows the complete balloon).
- `out/permit-filled.pdf` — verified after save: each value appears exactly once in page text (Tidewater Studio, 2026-12-05, North Cove Lawn, about 40) and `pypdf` `get_fields()` returns `None`, i.e. no editable form fields remain.
- Originals `launch.jpg`, `permit-form.pdf`, `event-details.txt` untouched (opened read-only).
- No browser tabs, windows or apps were opened, so nothing to close.

## Assumptions
- **Date format:** Ines wrote "Saturday 5 December 2026" but the form label says "Event date (YYYY-MM-DD)", so I entered `2026-12-05` — the form's requested format wins.
- **Attendees:** "about 40" entered verbatim from Ines's note rather than a rounded number.
- **Crop placement:** anchored to the right edge to keep the balloon (upper-right of the scene) fully inside; the small white cloud clipped at the left edge is not the subject.

## How I know it is right
- Image: pixel scan measured the balloon's extent before cropping; output reloaded programmatically (size) and visually inspected (balloon complete, circular, basket visible).
- PDF: post-save verification via two independent libraries — PyMuPDF page text shows each value once in the field positions, and pypdf reports no form fields, proving the answers are no longer editable.
